key_points.point: Net income fell 51%, from $3,314.6M to $1,635.3M. Diluted EPS fell from $6.55 to $3.28 and net income as a share of revenue fell from 26.9% to 17.3%. The filing attributes the drop to a $1,790.3M fall in operating income and a $40.3M rise in nonoperating expense, partly offset by a $151.4M lower tax provision.

Revenue fell 23%, from $12,305.5M to $9,427.2M, mainly because of weaker macroeconomic trends. The drop was sharpest in Industrial (-35%), where customers cut their inventory, and in Communications (-33%), because of the timing of infrastructure deployment. Automotive (-2%) and Consumer (-1%) fell less as reduced consumer spending weakened demand. Revenue fell in every region.
Gross margin fell $2,495.9M (32%). Gross margin % dropped 690 bp, from 64.0% to 57.1%, mainly because of lower factory utilization as customer demand fell, plus an unfavorable product mix.

Lower operating expenses partly offset the gross margin loss: SMG&A fell $204.9M (lower variable compensation, salary and benefits, and discretionary spending), amortization fell $204.8M (some acquired intangibles became fully amortized in 2023), R&D fell $172.3M (lower variable compensation) and special charges fell $123.5M (lower Q4 2023 Plan charges). The extra week in 53-week fiscal 2024 partly offset these cuts. Operating income still fell $1,790.3M (47%), and operating margin went from 31.1% to 21.6%.
Nonoperating expense rose $40.3M (19%), to $255.5M, because of higher interest expense on debt and lower net gains from other investments, partly offset by higher interest income.

The income tax provision fell $151.4M (52%), to $142.1M, which partly offset the decline. The effective tax rate was about the same (8.0% vs 8.1%) because pretax income was earned mainly in Ireland at a 12.5% rate. Fiscal 2023 had also included an $81.7M discrete tax benefit.

Customer inventory: Industrial revenue fell 35%, from $6,611.8M to $4,314.3M, as customers cut their inventory balances. This was a main reason total revenue fell 23%. Industrial's share of revenue fell from 54% to 46%.
The Industrial decline also cut the distributor channel's share of revenue from 61% to 58%, with distributor revenue falling from $7,534.9M to $5,505.8M. Distributors buy products to resell them.

Factory utilization: gross margin % fell 690 bp, from 64.0% to 57.1%, and gross margin fell $2,495.9M. The main causes were lower factory utilization as customer demand fell, plus an unfavorable product mix.

Company inventory fell 12%, from $1,642.2M to $1,447.7M, as the company worked to balance manufacturing production, demand and inventory levels. Inventory levels depend on the need to support forecast demand and on gaps between forecast and actual demand.
Days cost of sales in inventory rose from 125 to 139, calculated on average balances and including Maxim acquisition accounting adjustments. Inventory fell more slowly than cost of sales.

Working capital: operating cash flow fell from $4,817.6M to $3,852.5M because of lower adjusted net income, partly offset by changes in working capital, including the lower inventory and receivables balances.

At November 2, 2024, the company held $2.4B in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, about $1.3B of it in the US and the rest in foreign subsidiaries. The holdings are highly liquid (money market funds, corporate and bank obligations) and placed with high-credit-rating counterparties. Management does not expect repatriation restrictions or taxes to materially affect liquidity.
Management believes existing liquidity, future operating cash and available financing will cover operations, capex, R&D and dividends for at least the next twelve months.

Operating cash flow stayed strong at $3,852.5M, and rose to 41% of revenue from 39%. It was still down from $4,817.6M because of lower net income adjusted for noncash items, partly offset by working capital changes.
Cash used for investing fell to $1,104.9M from $1,266.4M, mainly because of lower capex. Cash used for financing fell to $1,714.4M from $4,063.8M, mainly because of lower share buybacks.
Signs of pressure: revenue fell 23% and net income fell 51%. Nonoperating expense rose because of higher interest expense on debt obligations, partly offset by higher interest income.

Working capital: accounts receivable fell 9% and inventory fell 12%, but days sales outstanding rose from 48 to 54 and days in inventory rose from 125 to 139. Current liabilities fell to $3.0B from $3.2B because of lower accrued liabilities and current debt, partly offset by higher income taxes payable.
